## Understanding Supercomputing and Researcher Demand

::: {style="margin-top: 30px;"}

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 0 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
What is Supercomputing (HPC)?
</div>

High-performance computing (HPC) uses **many processors working together** to solve complex problems, run simulations, and analyse large datasets at a scale that ordinary computers cannot easily achieve.

**What makes it different?** Supercomputers combine thousands of CPU cores, often supported by GPUs, to perform calculations **in parallel**.

**Research applications:** Climate modelling, weather forecasting, drug discovery, and engineering simulations.

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 12px 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Understanding Researcher Demand
</div>

- [**Demand (Requested)**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Computing resources researchers **request** for their research.
- [**Allocated**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Computing resources facilities **provide** to researchers.
- [**Unmet demand**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: The portion of requests **not fulfilled**, when the measures are comparable.

::: {style="margin-top: 10px; padding: 8px 14px; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; background-color: #F2F7FB; font-size: 0.85em;"}

**Important:** Historical demand is not always directly observed. Some values are estimated using allocations or proxies, so the forecasts represent **planning scenarios rather than exact predictions**.

:::

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.48em; color: #666; margin-top: 8px;"}

Source: [@ibm_hpc; @NCMAS2026]

:::

## Research Objective and Scope

::: {style="margin-top: 30px;"}

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 0 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Research question
</div>

How is demand for Australia's national research supercomputing infrastructure **projected to evolve through 2030?**

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 12px 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Project objectives
</div>

1. [**Compile and integrate**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} historical computing data from NCI, Pawsey, and supporting research datasets.
2. [**Standardise and harmonise**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} resource units, reporting periods, and research classifications.
3. [**Develop and evaluate**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} forecasting models using time-series cross-validation.
4. [**Forecast demand**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} for overall HPC, CPU, and GPU resources through 2030.
5. [**Assess alternative scenarios**]{style="color: #006DAE;"} for computing demand and Fields of Research (FoR).

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 12px 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Planning purpose
</div>

Provide **evidence-informed demand projections** to support long-term planning for Australia's national research computing infrastructure.

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.48em; color: #666; margin-top: 8px;"}

Source: [@HPCInternshipBrief]. Project scope and methodology were refined based on data availability, coverage, and comparability.

:::


## How Is Supercomputing Demand Measured?

::: {style="margin-top: 30px;"}

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 0 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Three Key Measurements
</div>

- [**CPU core-hours**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: CPU cores × computing hours.
- [**GPU-hours**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: GPUs × computing hours.
- [**Service units (SU)**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: System-specific accounting units; overall HPC is reported in **kSU (thousands of SU)**.

<div style="height: 12px;"></div>

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 12px 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Historical Comparability
</div>

- **Accounting rules vary** across computing systems, facilities, and reporting years.
- **Official conversion factors** are prioritised; documented assumptions are used where necessary.
- **Measurement uncertainty remains** and affects the interpretation of forecasts.

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

::: {style="padding: 8px 14px; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; background-color: #F2F7FB; font-size: 0.85em;"}

**Key takeaway:** Historical resource measures are not automatically comparable. This project harmonises them using documented conversion assumptions.

:::

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.48em; color: #666; margin-top: 8px;"}

Sources: [@NCMAS2026Info; @NCMAS2026; @NCMAS2020Info]. Conversion assumptions and limitations: project data harmonisation methodology.

:::

## Data Sources and Historical Coverage

::: {style="margin-top: 30px;"}

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 0 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Primary Data Sources
</div>

- [**NCI**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: National Computational Infrastructure. Historical reports and computing allocations.
- [**Pawsey**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre. Historical reports and computing allocations.
- [**NCMAS**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: National Computational Merit Allocation Scheme. Annual allocation outcomes.

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 12px 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Historical Analytical Coverage
</div>

- **Overall HPC:** 2014 - 2026, in thousands of service units (**kSU**).
- **CPU:** 2014 - 2026, in million CPU core-hours.
- **GPU:** 2022 - 2026, in million GPU-hours.
- **Fields of Research (FoR):** 2014 - 2026, historical research-field **allocation shares**, not directly observed FoR demand.

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

::: {style="padding: 8px 14px; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; background-color: #F2F7FB; font-size: 0.85em;"}

**Data limitation:** Historical series combine reported observations, derived estimates, and proxies. Data availability and comparability vary across facilities and years.

:::

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.48em; color: #666; margin-top: 8px;"}

Sources: [@NCI201314; @NCIAllocations202021; @Pawsey201617; @NCMAS2026]. Coverage and harmonisation: this project's data preparation methodology.

:::

<strong>What does this mean?</strong>

<ul>
<li>Allocation is mostly directly reported.</li>
<li>Demand combines direct observations, derived values, and proxies.</li>
<li>Historical records are not fully comparable across years.</li>
</ul>

</div>

<div class="prov-panel" style="margin-top: 10px; background: #FFF5EB;">

<strong>Main limitations</strong>

<ul>
<li>Different units and accounting rules.</li>
<li>Changes in reporting scope.</li>
<li>Historical conversion assumptions.</li>
<li>Incomplete CPU/GPU separation.</li>
</ul>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div class="prov-takeaway">
<strong>Key takeaway:</strong> Historical demand contains more estimated values than allocation. Forecasts should therefore be interpreted as planning scenarios, subject to historical measurement uncertainty.
</div>

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.3
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: center

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# Load harmonised historical dataset
annual_converted <- readRDS(
  "../assets/data/data converted/annual_demand_allocation_converted.rds"
)

# Load original GPU historical scenarios
historical_gpu_scenarios <- readRDS(
  "../assets/data/data converted/historical_gpu_scenarios.rds"
)

# Verify scenario coverage
stopifnot(
  nrow(historical_gpu_scenarios) == 8,
  identical(
    sort(as.integer(historical_gpu_scenarios$year)),
    2014:2021
  )
)

# Prepare historical series
historical_plot <- annual_converted |>
  transmute(
    year = as.integer(year),

    `Overall HPC|Demand` = demand_ksu / 1e6,
    `Overall HPC|Allocation` = allocation_ksu / 1e6,

    `CPU|Demand` = demand_cpu_core_hours / 1e6,
    `CPU|Allocation` = allocation_cpu_core_hours / 1e6,

    `GPU|Demand` = demand_gpu_hours / 1e6,
    `GPU|Allocation` = allocation_gpu_hours / 1e6
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -year,
    names_to = c("resource", "measure"),
    names_sep = "\\|",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(
    resource = factor(
      resource,
      levels = c("Overall HPC", "CPU", "GPU"),
      labels = c(
        "Overall HPC (million kSU)",
        "CPU (million core-hours)",
        "GPU (million GPU-hours)"
      )
    ),
    measure = factor(
      measure,
      levels = c("Demand", "Allocation")
    )
  )

# Prepare GPU low/high scenario bands, 2014–2021
gpu_uncertainty_data <- historical_gpu_scenarios |>
  select(
    year,
    demand_gpu_hours_low,
    demand_gpu_hours_high,
    allocation_gpu_hours_low,
    allocation_gpu_hours_high
  ) |>
  filter(
    year >= 2014,
    year <= 2021
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -year,
    names_to = c("measure", ".value"),
    names_pattern =
      "(demand|allocation)_(gpu_hours_low|gpu_hours_high)"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    measure = recode(
      measure,
      demand = "Demand",
      allocation = "Allocation"
    ),
    measure = factor(
      measure,
      levels = c("Demand", "Allocation")
    ),
    resource = factor(
      "GPU (million GPU-hours)",
      levels = levels(historical_plot$resource)
    ),
    gpu_hours_low = gpu_hours_low / 1e6,
    gpu_hours_high = gpu_hours_high / 1e6
  )

# Create plot
ggplot() +

  # GPU scenario uncertainty bands (2014–2021)
  geom_ribbon(
    data = gpu_uncertainty_data,
    aes(
      x = year,
      ymin = gpu_hours_low,
      ymax = gpu_hours_high,
      fill = measure,
      group = measure
    ),
    alpha = 0.18,
    colour = NA
  ) +

  # Solid lines:
  # All HPC and CPU years, plus GPU 2022–2026
  geom_line(
    data = historical_plot |>
      filter(
        resource != "GPU (million GPU-hours)" |
          year >= 2022
      ),
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = value,
      colour = measure,
      group = interaction(resource, measure)
    ),
    linewidth = 1.15
  ) +

  # Dashed GPU historical scenarios (2014–2021)
  geom_line(
    data = historical_plot |>
      filter(
        resource == "GPU (million GPU-hours)",
        year <= 2021
      ),
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = value,
      colour = measure,
      group = measure
    ),
    linewidth = 1.15,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  # Grey dotted connectors:
  # 2021 scenario to 2022 reported/estimated data
  geom_line(
    data = historical_plot |>
      filter(
        resource == "GPU (million GPU-hours)",
        year %in% c(2021, 2022)
      ),
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = value,
      group = measure
    ),
    colour = "#999999",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    linetype = "dotted"
  ) +

  # Demand and allocation points
  geom_point(
    data = historical_plot,
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = value,
      colour = measure
    ),
    size = 1.8
  ) +

  # GPU data transition divider
  geom_vline(
    data = data.frame(
      resource = factor(
        "GPU (million GPU-hours)",
        levels = levels(historical_plot$resource)
      ),
      boundary = 2021.5
    ),
    aes(xintercept = boundary),
    linetype = "dotted",
    colour = "#888888",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  # Three resource panels
  facet_wrap(
    ~resource,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  # Colours
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Demand" = "#006DAE",
      "Allocation" = "#E69F00"
    )
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Demand" = "#006DAE",
      "Allocation" = "#E69F00"
    )
  ) +

  # Axes
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2014, 2017, 2020, 2023, 2026)
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +

  # Labels
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = NULL,
    colour = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +

  guides(
    fill = "none"
  ) +

  # Theme
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "#17324D"
    ),
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#EAF2F9",
      colour = NA
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 10
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.3, "cm"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 8, 2, 8)
  )
```

:::

<div class="slide7-insights">

<div class="slide7-insight">

<strong>Overall HPC</strong>

<p>Reconstructed demand rose <strong>43.3%</strong> in 2026; official NCMAS growth was approximately <strong>24%</strong>.</p>

<p>Allocation remained near <strong>0.87 million kSU</strong>, widening the demand–allocation gap.</p>

</div>

<div class="slide7-insight">

<strong>CPU</strong>

<p>Demand increased sharply after 2020, reaching approximately <strong>1.25 billion core-hours</strong> in 2026.</p>

<p>Allocation remained near <strong>530 million core-hours</strong>, indicating a widening resource gap.</p>

</div>

<div class="slide7-insight">

<strong>GPU</strong>

<p>Demand reached approximately <strong>3.0 million GPU-hours</strong> in 2026, more than twice allocation.</p>

<p><strong>2014 - 2021:</strong> Historical scenarios. <strong>2022 - 2026:</strong> Mixed reported and estimated data.</p>

</div>

</div>

<div class="slide7-note">
<strong>Notes:</strong> GPU dashed lines and shaded bands for 2014 - 2021 represent assumption-based historical scenarios, not statistical confidence intervals. Historical values include reported and estimated data. The 2025 HPC demand estimate affects the reconstructed 2026 growth rate. The 2026 overall HPC allocation excludes 12,000 kSU awarded to Setonix Q. Panel units and scales differ.
</div>

.slide8-panel-title { background: #EAF3F9; color: #17324D; font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; padding: 3px 8px; text-align: center; }
.slide8-main .cell, .slide8-main .cell-output, .slide8-main .cell-output-display,
.slide8-periods .cell, .slide8-periods .cell-output, .slide8-periods .cell-output-display { width: 100% !important; max-width: 100% !important; margin: 0 !important; }
.slide8-main img, .slide8-periods img { display: block; width: 100% !important; max-width: 100% !important; height: auto; margin: 0 auto; }
.slide8-insight { background: #F2F7FB; border-left: 4px solid #006DAE; padding: 5px 10px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.15; margin-top: 3px; }
.slide8-note { font-size: 10px; color: #555; line-height: 1.15; margin-top: 3px; }
</style>

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(stringr)

# Load historical FoR data
for_converted <- readRDS(
  "../assets/data/data converted/field_of_research_converted.rds"
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(for_converted) == 133,
  identical(
    sort(unique(as.integer(for_converted$year))),
    2014:2026
  )
)

# Consistent colours
for_palette <- c(
  "Physical Sciences" = "#006DAE",
  "Chemical Sciences" = "#38A6D8",
  "Earth & Environmental Sciences" = "#279A8B",
  "Engineering & Technology" = "#E69F00",
  "Biological & Agricultural Sciences" = "#74B86A",
  "Medical & Health Sciences" = "#B77DBD",
  "Mathematics & Computing" = "#E27B66",
  "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment" = "#8B91A9",
  "Unclassified & Operational" = "#B7BEC7"
)

field_order <- names(for_palette)

# ----------------------------------------
# Overall: harmonised groups, 2014–2026
# ----------------------------------------

for_overall <- for_converted |>
  mutate(
    reported_clean = research_field_reported |>
      str_remove("^\\s*\\d{2}\\s+") |>
      str_to_lower() |>
      str_replace_all("&", " and ") |>
      str_squish(),

    field = case_when(
      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "physical sciences|radioastronomy|radio astronomy"
      ) ~ "Physical Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "chemical sciences"
      ) ~ "Chemical Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "earth|environmental|geoscien"
      ) ~ "Earth & Environmental Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "engineering|technology"
      ) ~ "Engineering & Technology",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "biological|agricultural|veterinary|food sciences"
      ) ~ "Biological & Agricultural Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "medical|health|biomedical|clinical"
      ) ~ "Medical & Health Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "mathematical|computing|information"
      ) ~ "Mathematics & Computing",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        paste0(
          "psychology|economics|history|archaeology|",
          "human society|language|communication|culture|",
          "philosophy|religious|built environment|design"
        )
      ) ~ "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "other|unreported|unclassified|pawsey operations"
      ) ~ "Unclassified & Operational",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(for_overall$field),
  n_distinct(for_overall$field) == 9
)

for_overall_plot <- for_overall |>
  group_by(year, field) |>
  summarise(
    allocation_share = sum(allocation_share_for),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ----------------------------------------
# Early period: FoR 2008, 2014–2020
# ----------------------------------------

for_early <- for_converted |>
  filter(between(year, 2014, 2020)) |>
  mutate(
    field = case_when(
      for_2008_division_code == "01" ~
        "Mathematics & Computing",

      for_2008_division_code == "02" ~
        "Physical Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code == "03" ~
        "Chemical Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code %in% c(
        "04", "05", "04 + 05"
      ) ~ "Earth & Environmental Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code %in% c(
        "06", "07"
      ) ~ "Biological & Agricultural Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code == "08" ~
        "Mathematics & Computing",

      for_2008_division_code %in% c(
        "09", "10", "09 + 10"
      ) ~ "Engineering & Technology",

      for_2008_division_code == "11" ~
        "Medical & Health Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code %in% c(
        "12", "21"
      ) ~ "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment",

      is.na(for_2008_division_code) ~
        "Unclassified & Operational",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

stopifnot(!anyNA(for_early$field))

for_early_plot <- for_early |>
  group_by(year, field) |>
  summarise(
    allocation_share = sum(allocation_share_for),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ----------------------------------------
# Later period: FoR 2020, 2021–2026
# ----------------------------------------

for_late <- for_converted |>
  filter(between(year, 2021, 2026)) |>
  mutate(
    field = case_when(
      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Engineering",
        "Engineering + Technology",
        "Technology — no direct FoR 2020 alignment"
      ) ~ "Engineering & Technology",

      for_standard_2020 == "Physical sciences" ~
        "Physical Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 == "Chemical sciences" ~
        "Chemical Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Earth sciences",
        "Environmental sciences",
        "Earth sciences + Environmental sciences"
      ) ~ "Earth & Environmental Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Biological sciences",
        "Agricultural, veterinary and food sciences"
      ) ~ "Biological & Agricultural Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Biomedical and clinical sciences",
        "Health sciences",
        "Biomedical and clinical sciences + Health sciences"
      ) ~ "Medical & Health Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Mathematical sciences",
        "Information and computing sciences"
      ) ~ "Mathematics & Computing",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Psychology",
        "Economics",
        "History, heritage and archaeology",
        "Language, communication and culture",
        "Philosophy and religious studies",
        "Human society",
        "Built environment and design"
      ) ~ "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment",

      for_standard_2020 == "Other / Unclassified" ~
        "Unclassified & Operational",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

stopifnot(!anyNA(for_late$field))

for_late_plot <- for_late |>
  group_by(year, field) |>
  summarise(
    allocation_share = sum(allocation_share_for),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Validate annual shares before plotting
for (dataset in list(for_overall_plot, for_early_plot, for_late_plot)) {
  totals <- dataset |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(total = sum(allocation_share), .groups = "drop")
  stopifnot(all(abs(totals$total - 1) < 1e-6))
}

# Consistent field order and include absent categories as 0 for period averages
prepare_for <- function(data) {
  data |>
    mutate(field = factor(field, levels = field_order)) |>
    complete(year, field, fill = list(allocation_share = 0))
}
for_overall_plot <- prepare_for(for_overall_plot)
for_early_plot <- prepare_for(for_early_plot)
for_late_plot <- prepare_for(for_late_plot)

for_early_average <- for_early_plot |>
  group_by(field) |>
  summarise(mean_share = mean(allocation_share), .groups = "drop")
for_late_average <- for_late_plot |>
  group_by(field) |>
  summarise(mean_share = mean(allocation_share), .groups = "drop")

top_early_period <- for_early_average |>
  slice_max(mean_share, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
top_late_period <- for_late_average |>
  slice_max(mean_share, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

# Match label positions to reverse stacking of geom_col
for_top_overall <- for_overall_plot |>
  arrange(year, field) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(ymid = cumsum(allocation_share) - allocation_share / 2) |>
  slice_max(allocation_share, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(label = percent(allocation_share, accuracy = 1))

short_field_labels <- c(
  "Physical Sciences" = "Physical Sciences",
  "Chemical Sciences" = "Chemical Sciences",
  "Earth & Environmental Sciences" = "Earth & Environmental",
  "Engineering & Technology" = "Engineering & Technology",
  "Biological & Agricultural Sciences" = "Biological & Agricultural",
  "Medical & Health Sciences" = "Medical & Health",
  "Mathematics & Computing" = "Mathematics & Computing",
  "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment" = "Social Sciences & Humanities",
  "Unclassified & Operational" = "Unclassified & Operational"
)

plot_for_overall <- function(data) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = factor(year), y = allocation_share, fill = field)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.83, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
    geom_text(
      data = for_top_overall,
      aes(x = factor(year), y = ymid, label = label),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = for_palette, limits = field_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"),
      legend.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.05, "cm"),
      plot.margin = margin(3, 6, 2, 6)
    )
}

plot_for_average <- function(data) {
  chart_data <- data |>
    arrange(mean_share) |>
    mutate(
      field_label = unname(short_field_labels[as.character(field)]),
      field_label = factor(field_label, levels = field_label)
    )

  ggplot(chart_data, aes(x = mean_share, y = field_label, fill = field)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.68) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = percent(mean_share, accuracy = 1)),
      hjust = -0.15, size = 2.8, colour = "#17324D", fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = for_palette, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = label_percent(),
      breaks = seq(0, 0.5, 0.1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(3, 12, 2, 3)
    )
}
```

## Model Development: Growth Assumptions & Sensitivity

<style>
.slide9 {
  width: 100%;
  margin-top: 5px;
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.25;
}

.slide9-intro {
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.3;
  margin-bottom: 15px;
}

.slide9-models {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 24px;
  margin-bottom: 18px;
}

.slide9-model {
  border-top: 3px solid #006DAE;
  padding: 10px 5px 3px;
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.3;
}

.slide9-model strong {
  color: #17324D;
}

.slide9-model p {
  margin: 6px 0;
}

.slide9-equation {
  font-size: 19px;
  color: #17324D;
  margin: 9px 0;
}

.slide9-section {
  color: #17324D;
  font-weight: 700;
  font-size: 19px;
  margin: 10px 0 8px;
}

.slide9-reason {
  font-size: 15px;
  line-height: 1.3;
  margin-bottom: 12px;
}

.slide9 .slide9-results {
  width: 100%;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.2;
  margin: 0;
}

.slide9 .slide9-results th {
  color: #17324D;
  border-bottom: 2px solid #17324D;
  padding: 9px 12px;
  text-align: left;
}

.slide9 .slide9-results td {
  padding: 9px 12px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #DDE5EC;
}

.slide9 .slide9-results td:first-child {
  font-weight: 700;
}

.slide9-finding {
  border-top: 2px solid #006DAE;
  margin-top: 14px;
  padding-top: 10px;
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.3;
}

.slide9-for {
  margin-top: 15px;
  font-size: 15px;
  line-height: 1.3;
}

.slide9-for strong {
  color: #17324D;
}

.slide9-note {
  font-size: 11px;
  color: #555;
  line-height: 1.3;
  margin-top: 11px;
}
</style>

::: {.slide9}

::: {.slide9-intro}
**Model rationale:** The annual demand series contain **13 observations for HPC and CPU (2014 to 2026)** and **5 observations for GPU (2022 to 2026)**. Linear and log-linear regression models were fitted to compare absolute and proportional growth assumptions using a limited number of observations.
:::

::: {.slide9-models}

::: {.slide9-model}
**Linear trend: Absolute growth**

::: {.slide9-equation}
$D_t = \alpha + \beta t + \varepsilon_t$
:::

Estimates the **absolute annual change** in demand. This provides a direct measure of additional computing resources required each year.
:::

::: {.slide9-model}
**Log-linear trend: Proportional growth**

::: {.slide9-equation}
$\log(D_t) = \alpha + \beta t + \varepsilon_t$
:::

Estimates **proportional annual growth**. This allows demand to increase at a compounded rate rather than by a fixed amount.
:::

:::

::: {.slide9-section}
Sensitivity analysis: Influence of 2026
:::

::: {.slide9-reason}
The reconstructed demand increases sharply in 2026. To assess whether this observation substantially influences the estimated growth rate, linear models were fitted both **including and excluding 2026**.
:::

| Resource | Excluding 2026 | Including 2026 | Change |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| **Overall HPC** | 144,357 kSU/year | **161,992 kSU/year** | **+12.2%** |
| **CPU** | 72.41M core-hours/year | **81.01M core-hours/year** | **+11.9%** |
| **GPU** | 0.012M GPU-hours/year | **0.172M GPU-hours/year** | Highly sensitive |

::: {.slide9-finding}
Including 2026 increases the estimated annual linear growth by approximately **12% for HPC and CPU**. GPU estimates are more sensitive because only five years of suitable data are available.
:::

::: {.slide9-for}
**Field of Research (FoR):** Historical allocation shares were used to develop research field scenarios. Separate demand regression models were not fitted because directly observed FoR demand data are unavailable.
:::

::: {.slide9-note}
**Notes:** GPU modelling uses data from 2022 to 2026 and excludes the assumption-based historical scenarios from 2014 to 2021. Sensitivity measures changes in fitted coefficients, not forecast accuracy. Model evaluation follows in Chapter 8.
:::

:::


## Model Evaluation: Forecast Accuracy & Diagnostics

<style>

  width: 100%;
  margin-top: 6px;
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.28;
}

.slide10-intro {
  font-size: 16px;
  margin-bottom: 12px;
}

.slide10-chart {
  width: 100%;
  margin-top: 4px;
}

.slide10-chart .cell-output,
.slide10-chart .cell-output-display {

  max-width: 100% !important;
}

.slide10-chart img {
  display: block;
  width: 100% !important;
  height: auto;
  margin: 0 auto;
}

.slide10-findings {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 14px;
  margin-top: 10px;
}

.slide10-finding {
  background: #F2F7FB;
  border-top: 3px solid #006DAE;
  padding: 11px 13px;
  font-size: 14px;
  line-height: 1.3;
}

  color: #17324D;
}

.slide10-finding p {
  margin: 6px 0;
}

.slide10-conclusion {
  border-top: 2px solid #006DAE;
  padding-top: 10px;
  margin-top: 15px;
  font-size: 16px;
  line-height: 1.3;
}

.slide10-note {
  margin-top: 12px;
  font-size: 11px;
  color: #555;
  line-height: 1.3;
}
</style>

::: {.slide10}

::: {.slide10-intro}
**Evaluation approach:** Four models were compared using expanding-window, one-step-ahead cross-validation: **naïve, drift, linear and log-linear**. Accuracy was measured using RMSE and MAE on the original demand scale.
:::

::: {.slide10-chart}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: center

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

accuracy_data <- data.frame(
  resource = rep(
    c("Overall HPC", "CPU", "GPU"),
    each = 4
  ),
  model = rep(
    c("Naïve", "Drift", "Linear", "Log-linear"),
    times = 3
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    378864, 314588, 290898, 511614,
    260.05, 242.61, 157.72, 160.18,
    0.441, 0.537, 0.729, 0.719
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    resource = factor(
      resource,
      levels = c("Overall HPC", "CPU", "GPU"),
      labels = c(
        "Overall HPC (thousand kSU)",
        "CPU (million core-hours)",
        "GPU (million GPU-hours)"
      )
    ),
    model = factor(
      model,
      levels = c("Naïve", "Drift", "Linear", "Log-linear")
    ),
    plot_rmse = if_else(
      resource == "Overall HPC (thousand kSU)",
      RMSE / 1000,
      RMSE
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(resource) |>
  mutate(
    best = plot_rmse == min(plot_rmse),
    label = if_else(
      resource == "Overall HPC (thousand kSU)",
      format(round(plot_rmse, 1), nsmall = 1),
      format(round(plot_rmse, 2), nsmall = 2)
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(
  accuracy_data,
  aes(x = model, y = plot_rmse, fill = best)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    vjust = -0.45,
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold",
    colour = "#17324D"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ resource,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "TRUE" = "#006DAE",
      "FALSE" = "#A9CDE3"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.17))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Cross-validation RMSE"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "#17324D"
    ),
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#EAF3F9",
      colour = NA
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 10,
      angle = 30,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 12, 5, 5)
  )
```
:::

<div class="slide10-findings">

<div class="slide10-finding">
<strong>Overall HPC</strong>
<p><strong>Linear</strong> achieved the lowest RMSE of <strong>290,898 kSU</strong> and MAE of <strong>198,295 kSU</strong>.</p>
<p>Evaluated over six years, 2021 to 2026.</p>
</div>

<div class="slide10-finding">
<strong>CPU</strong>
<p><strong>Linear</strong> had the lowest RMSE at <strong>157.72 million core-hours</strong>.</p>
<p><strong>Log-linear</strong> had the lowest MAE at <strong>133.74 million core-hours</strong>.</p>
</div>

<div class="slide10-finding">
<strong>GPU</strong>
<p><strong>Naïve</strong> had the lowest RMSE at <strong>0.441 million GPU-hours</strong>.</p>
<p>Only two evaluation years, 2025 and 2026, limit confidence in the ranking.</p>
</div>

</div>

::: {.slide10-conclusion}
**Key finding:** Linear trends performed best on RMSE for overall HPC and CPU, while the naïve benchmark performed best for GPU. Model selection must also consider data limitations, sensitivity to 2026 and suitability for forecasting through 2030.
:::

::: {.slide10-note}
**Notes:** RMSE is shown in thousand kSU for overall HPC and million hours for CPU and GPU. Panel scales differ. Overall HPC and CPU use six one-step-ahead errors; GPU uses two. Cross-validation accuracy does not establish long-term forecast reliability. Source: Project model evaluation, Chapter 8.
:::
